issue_reference: Assigned in the registration pull request rather than guessed in advance.
purpose: The final run's curve went flat at about episode 7,000 and its agent reached parity with rule_based_agent: score -0.232 [-0.793, +0.282] paired over 100 worlds, ahead on coins (+0.393 [+0.130, +0.645]) and behind on kills (-0.125 [-0.217, -0.038]). Score here is coins plus five times kills, so the kill gap is what separates us from the heuristic. This run continues from that agent instead of from the Task 3 incumbent, and asks whether facing the line-up we are actually judged against closes the gap.
hypothesis: Our agent has never faced three opponents that bomb it. Two of its three training partners are harmless: coin_collector_agent never places a bomb and peaceful_agent does nothing. In training it takes 0.21 to 0.26 kills per episode and scores 4.04; against three rule_based_agents it takes 0.105 and scores 3.17. We expect the hard line-up to transfer better to the tournament suite. We expect it to cost coin collection, which is the risk the opponent-mixture screen recorded, and the control arm lets us see that cost and decline it.

prior_evidence.training_opponents: Tested twice from the Task 3 incumbent and flat both times. The opponent-mixture screen (6 replicas x 400 episodes) measured mixed minus hard at -0.075 [-0.729, +0.625] on the tournament suite, and the line-up trajectory at the selected learning rate (3 replicas x 2,400 episodes) measured -0.250 [-0.975, +0.400] with 0 of 3 replicas beating the incumbent in either arm. Neither run beat the incumbent at all, so neither is a test of this factor in a regime where the agent is already good. That is what this run adds: a warm start from an agent that is 0.728 [0.172, 1.265] above the incumbent, and six times the episodes.
prior_evidence.kill_reward: Deliberately not the factor under test. Raising the attributable elimination reward from +5 to +20 was tried twice and did nothing: +0.010 [-0.080, +0.105] eliminations in the elimination-reward screen, +0.005 [-0.085, +0.100] under strong approach pressure in the compensated comparison. The hunting diagnosis explains why. A bomb aimed at an opponent with no crate in its blast books the -0.5 wasteful-bomb penalty immediately and with certainty, while the kill arrives four steps later, discounted by gamma^4 to about 0.66 of its value, and only if the opponent fails to walk away. At the conversion we measure, about one kill per hundred attack steps, the expected value of attacking stays negative whatever the kill is worth.
prior_evidence.safe_attack_penalty: Removing that penalty for framework-confirmed safe, crate-free attacks was tested over 50,000 training episodes and moved eliminations by 0 percentage points [0, 0]. It is not retried here.
prior_evidence.approach_shaping: Potential scale 3.0 raised attack exposure more than any other setting and lost score and collection against its control, so the shared potential scale stays where the final run had it.
prior_evidence.learning_rate: The dose ladder selected 0.0002 and the final run compared 0.0002 against 0.0001 over 8,000 episodes with no separation on the tournament suite: halved minus control +0.083 [-0.450, +0.550]. Both arms here use 0.0001, the gentler of the two, because this run fine-tunes an agent we intend to keep rather than training one from scratch.
prior_evidence.conservation: The line-up trajectory recorded the mechanism this run has to overcome: as the agent learns to stop destroying itself, self-kills fell 0.700 to 0.442 and survival rose 0.225 to 0.467 while eliminations fell 0.175 to 0.092, leaving score flat across a four-fold range of budget. Our own run reproduced it at ten times the scale. If the hard line-up only trades kills for safety again, this run will be flat too, and that is the outcome the control arm and the fallback checkpoint are there for.

warm_start.source_artifact: control-r1 milestone-008000.pt of the 2026-09-17 final training run
warm_start.selection_rule: Fixed in advance and not chosen on performance: the first job alphabetically, at the newest milestone every job had reached. Checkpoint ranking on 100 worlds is indistinguishable from noise (observed spread of checkpoint means 0.193 against a standard error of 0.211, split-half rank correlation -0.22), so there is nothing to select on and picking the best-looking one would only be a winner's curse.
warm_start.migration: Weights and target network copied verbatim, verified tensor by tensor. Episode counter zeroed, replay buffer emptied and optimizer state cleared, which is what bind() requires of an initialization and what lets each replica seed its own exploration stream.

intervention.baseline_shared_by_every_arm: all_weights, learning rate 0.0001, kill reward 5.0, the episode-mixture exploration schedule at period five, and the warm start above
intervention.persistence: Milestones every 1,000 episodes and a durable resume every 25.
intervention.registered_risk: The hard line-up failed all three retention gates in the opponent-mixture screen at learning rate 0.0005. We watch collection on coin-heaven and loot-crate at every milestone, and a hard arm that loses collection without gaining score is declined.
intervention.milestone_evaluation: Every milestone of both arms is compared against the warm-start agent itself on fresh worlds, paired per world. The warm-start agent is the incumbent for this run and the artifact we ship if nothing here beats it.

random_episode_schedule: Per arm: for each block of `random_episode_period` episodes, random.Random(agent_seed + 168000000 + block_index).randrange(period) selects one fully random episode and the rest are greedy.

classic-rule-based.role: development; every registered gate and the selection contrast read this suite

primary_endpoint: Mean native score per game on the tournament suite, against the warm-start agent rather than the Task 3 incumbent, paired on the world. The incumbent is no longer the relevant baseline: we already beat it and we would not ship it.

uncertainty.method: hierarchical paired bootstrap over replicas and shared worlds
uncertainty.family: one test family per arm judged under the corrected rule, the control included; the promotion rule is conjunctive, so only the arm count is Bonferroni-adjusted
uncertainty.role: registered decision input, not a post-hoc description

selection: We ship an artifact from this run only if it beats the warm-start agent on the tournament suite on fresh worlds, paired per world and per checkpoint, with the score point estimate at least zero and the interval's lower bound above -0.15. Otherwise the warm-start agent ships. The pipeline's own promotion screen is expected to veto everything through the invalid-action gate, which compares each trained artifact against the untrained reference with no tolerance and which every one of our 18 measured milestones already fails; that gate is recorded, not relaxed.
scientific_gates: Original cumulative Task 1/2/3 requirements are unchanged; this run cannot retrospectively establish any of them.
known_gate_defect: Judged under promotion rule version 2: the invalid-action gate compares each trained artifact against the unchanged reference rather than demanding a global zero the reference itself cannot reach, frozen_online_weights reports not-applicable for arms registered to move the weights, and promotion and selection key on score, the registered primary endpoint.

machine_allocation.training: 6 concurrent workers, one torch thread each
machine_allocation.latency: one worker on an otherwise idle machine; the only latency source

authorization: Julius (1BlauNitrox) asked for a continuation run on 18 September 2026 after reading the flat trajectory and the rule_based comparison, and accepted that the previous run stops at about 9,500 of its registered 24,000 episodes.
